citation: Zhang Qing, Liu Xingchen, Liu Yanyan, et al. Nasal and cutaneous mucormycosis in two patients with lymphoma after chemotherapy and target therapy: Early detection by metagenomic next-generation sequencing: A case report and literature review. Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology, 2022.
study_design: Case report (2 cases) plus literature review
study_period: June 2021 to February 2022 (case 1 admitted 27 June 2021; case 2 admitted 18 October 2021)

population.population_description: Two patients with hematologic malignancies (lymphoma) with nasal/cutaneous mucormycosis after chemotherapy/ibrutinib, diagnosed by peripheral blood mNGS and confirmed by secretion culture
population.haemato_subtypes: 1 T-lymphoblastic lymphoma (10-year-old girl), 1 chronic lymphocytic leukemia (64-year-old man on ibrutinib)

neutropenic_status: Case 1 febrile neutropenia with ANC 0.02 x 10^9/L during induction; case 2 not neutropenic (ANC 21.15 x 10^9/L)

index_test.platform_or_panel: mNGS on MGISEQ-2000 (MGI, Shenzhen); Genskey library kit; ~12,000-genome database

reference_standard: Clinical diagnosis confirmed by fungal culture of local secretions (case 1: fluorescent staining of nasal secretions showing pauci-septate hyphae + multidisciplinary clinical diagnosis; case 2: secretion culture grew Mucor)

diagnostic_yield.basis: 2/2 PB mNGS positive for Mucorales (Lichtheimia ramosa 3330 reads; Mucor irregularis 55 reads)

additional_yield_vs_conventional: Initial blood/secretion cultures and G/GM tests were negative before mNGS; mNGS preceded culture confirmation; 'Within 48 h, the mNGS results were released' while subsequent secretion culture confirmed
therapy_change: Case 1: switched to amphotericin B cholesterol sulfate complex + nasal amphotericin + debridement; case 2: antifungal adjusted to ABCD after mNGS, plus ganciclovir
mortality_or_outcomes: Both patients recovered ('both patients obtained successful outcomes'); no return of mucormycosis until Feb 2022 (case 1); skin wound completely healed (case 2)

quality_flags.overlap_risk: None - isolated cases; literature review table of other mucormycosis mNGS cases is not original data

quadas2_notes: n=2; no applicability for pooled diagnostic accuracy; reference standard partly clinical (multidisciplinary diagnosis) plus culture.

evidence_quotes.quote: Here we used mNGS to timely diagnose an infection with Lichtheimia ramosa and Mucor irregularis in two patients with hematologic malignancies
Within 48 h, the mNGS results were released: M. irregularis, human betaherpesvirus, human alphaherpesvirus, and Alphatorquevirus were detected
Fungus | Lichtheimia | 3414 | Lichtheimia ramosa | 3330 ... 2 | PB | Fungus | Mucor | 55 | Mucor irregularis | 55
The subsequent fungal culture of the secretion revealed Mucor growth, confirming the cutaneous mucormycosis.
Following treatment with amphotericin B cholesteryl sulfate complex, the symptoms were reduced significantly, and both patients obtained successful outcomes.

exclusion_reason: Case report (n=2 patients, below threshold); no 2x2 or yield denominator.
